```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Price headroom is better supported in A. Published comparables run $49–$349/mo (Expiration Reminder) and $500–$800/location/yr (ClearBot). B's entry pricing has been pushed to $5–$12.90/mo, and its dominant incumbent (473 reviews, 4.9 stars) has a free plan. At B's price, one lost customer or a refund wipes out the 90-day signal.",
    "A's demand evidence comes from people with concrete money at stake. A therapist weighs a $440 renewal, and a one-person engineering firm tracks license and COA dates alongside tax deadlines. These are identifiable, reachable niches, which suggests direct outreach to a single vertical could land a first paying customer without relying on the $87–$200 CPL paid channel.",
    "B's discovery problem blocks the 90-day goal directly. Incumbents hold 100–470+ reviews and 'Built for Shopify' badges, and the only paid-channel evidence says roughly $500/mo for 90 days is needed before payback data even emerges. That consumes the whole window.",
    "A can shrink its scope to fit a solo operator. A tracking-only, single-vertical MVP matches the cheapest published competitor tier and avoids the 50-state rule-change monitoring the brief flags as unsustainable. B's scope is already minimal, and the brief suggests its photo-only approach is technically behind where the market is heading, so there is no comparable way to narrow into advantage.",
    "B carries an unresolved retention question that A does not. B asks whether its revenue is recurring or a one-time catalog cleanup. A's renewal deadlines recur by nature, which fits a subscription.",
    "A has real weaknesses of its own. Its Google Ads CPL figures come from what the brief itself calls an AI-aggregated blog. Its affiliate data is an adjacent-market proxy. Its own evidence shows sufferers mostly use spreadsheets rather than buying tools. A wins on relative position, not strength."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not show willingness to pay a new entrant. Two of the three items are generic Reddit complaints that descriptions are time-consuming, and the third is a testimonial for an incumbent competitor (AltText.ai). Together they support the existing category leaders, not a new app. The acquisition evidence is similarly thin: a single agency case study (Helium) whose 14x ROAS took years to reach.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with no direct evidence that anyone would pay a new solo entrant. A wins mainly on higher published price anchors, reachable vertical niches, and recurring need. It is still exposed to spreadsheet inertia, unverified CPL figures, and liability for data inaccuracy. The pick depends on keeping A's MVP to tracking only, without rule-change monitoring."
}
```
